From e0f3b803d74277677697bdf5b5e4c28766cfbc93 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Richard Weinberger <richard@nod.at>
Date: Tue, 26 Oct 2010 14:21:13 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] um: fix global timer issue when using CONFIG_NO_HZ

commit 482db6df1746c4fa7d64a2441d4cb2610249c679 upstream.

This fixes a issue which was introduced by fe2cc53e ("uml: track and make
up lost ticks").

timeval_to_ns() returns long long and not int.  Due to that UML's timer
did not work properlt and caused timer freezes.

Signed-off-by: Richard Weinberger <richard@nod.at>
Acked-by: Pekka Enberg <penberg@kernel.org>
Cc: Jeff Dike <jdike@addtoit.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Paul Gortmaker <paul.gortmaker@windriver.com>

diff --git a/arch/um/os-Linux/time.c b/arch/um/os-Linux/time.c
index dec5678fc17..6e3359d6a83 100644
--- a/arch/um/os-Linux/time.c
+++ b/arch/um/os-Linux/time.c
@@ -60,7 +60,7 @@ static inline long long timeval_to_ns(const struct timeval *tv)
 long long disable_timer(void)
 {
 	struct itimerval time = ((struct itimerval) { { 0, 0 }, { 0, 0 } });
-	int remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
+	long long remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
 
 	if (setitimer(ITIMER_VIRTUAL, &time, &time) < 0)
 		printk(UM_KERN_ERR "disable_timer - setitimer failed, "
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/um/os-Linux/time.c`**
   - The type of the variable `remain` was changed from `int` to `long long`. This change ensures that the variable can hold larger values, which is necessary because the function `timeval_to_ns()` returns a `long long` type. 
   - This modification is crucial for the proper functioning of the timer in UML (User Mode Linux), particularly when the `CONFIG_NO_HZ` configuration is used.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `arch/um/os-Linux/time.c` directly addresses a bug related to the timer functionality in UML. The original issue stemmed from the incorrect handling of timer values due to type mismatch, which led to timer freezes. By changing the type of `remain` to `long long`, the patch ensures that the timer can correctly process the values returned by `timeval_to_ns()`, thereby fixing the global timer issue when using the `CONFIG_NO_HZ` configuration. This change is a direct response to the problem introduced by a previous commit (fe2cc53e) that aimed to track and make up lost ticks.

        Root cause:
        The bug was caused by a type mismatch where the variable `remain` was declared as an `int`, while the function `timeval_to_ns()` returns a `long long`. This mismatch led to improper handling of timer values, resulting in timer freezes in UML when using the `CONFIG_NO_HZ` configuration.

        um: fix global timer issue when using CONFIG_NO_HZ

commit 482db6df1746c4fa7d64a2441d4cb2610249c679 upstream.

This fixes a issue which was introduced by fe2cc53e ("uml: track and make
up lost ticks").

timeval_to_ns() returns long long and not int.  Due to that UML's timer
did not work properlt and caused timer freezes.

Signed-off-by: Richard Weinberger <richard@nod.at>
Acked-by: Pekka Enberg <penberg@kernel.org>
Cc: Jeff Dike <jdike@addtoit.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Paul Gortmaker <paul.gortmaker@windriver.com>  
        
        Patch:
         
 long long disable_timer(void)
 {
 	struct itimerval time = ((struct itimerval) { { 0, 0 }, { 0, 0 } });
-	int remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
+	long long remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
 
 	if (setitimer(ITIMER_VIRTUAL, &time, &time) < 0)
 		printk(UM_KERN_ERR "disable_timer - setitimer failed, "
 		       "errno = %d\n", errno);
 
 	remain = timeval_to_ns(&time.it_value);
 	if (remain > max)
 		remain = max;
 
 	return remain;
 }
